title: Cracks in the Register
briefing: An inspection model flags hundreds of apartment blocks as unsafe after heavy rain. Inspectors can visit only a fraction tonight.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Digital records accurately identify roof loading, but miss basement conversions and later changes to drainage.
private_intelligence.community: Tenants may not report cracks if inspection could trigger eviction; landlords and occupants need separate reporting routes.
private_intelligence.economy: Vacating every flagged building would consume the emergency lodging budget before engineering checks are complete.
private_intelligence.safety: Visible movement and jammed exits are stronger immediate warning signs than several high model scores.

choices.title: Vacate Broadly as a Precaution
choices.description: Provide temporary lodging for occupants of all high-risk blocks.
choices.consequence: Precaution reduces immediate exposure and reassures many tenants, but vacant buildings and lodging costs erode service capacity.

choices.title: Follow the Risk Register
choices.description: Send inspectors to the highest digitally scored buildings first.
choices.consequence: Registered structural risks receive quick attention, but excluded tenants lose trust and some unrecorded hazards persist.

choices.title: Combine Reports and Engineering
choices.description: Create protected tenant reporting with mobile engineer triage.
choices.consequence: More hidden hazards become visible and residents cooperate, while slower visits and extra staffing consume funds.
